description: Normative 2°C pathway: current policies to 2030, then abrupt global action; MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM 2.0.
pathwayDescription:
The Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) develops reference climate scenarios to help central banks, regulators, and financial institutions assess transition and physical risks associated with climate change. The Delayed Transition, MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM 2.0-M-R12 (DT MESSAGE)  scenario describes a world in which meaningful climate action is postponed until after 2030, followed by a rapid and disorderly policy tightening to meet long-term climate goals. This scenario assumes that governments initially maintain a trajectory close to current policies through the 2020s, with rising emissions and continued dependence on fossil fuels. As climate impacts intensify and policy pressure mounts, an abrupt transition occurs from the 2030s onward, involving steep carbon prices, accelerated technology deployment, and faster-than-planned phaseout of high-emitting assets.

The DT MESSAGE scenario corresponds to a late yet forceful transition pathway, limiting global warming to around 1.8°C by 2100, comparable to NGFS’s Below 2°C Scenario (B2C MESSAGE), but with higher costs due to the delayed start.

This scenario is one of seven scenarios published by NGFS. Note that all NGFS scenarios are produced using three different Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs): REMIND-MAgPIE, MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM, and GCAM. These IAMs share the common assumptions that define each scenario, but may offer different projections based on underlying model structure. Technical users may wish to consult NGFS documentation to determine if a specific IAM best fits their applications.

coreDrivers.policies: Carbon price: the shadow carbon price reaches 2 US$2010/tCO2 in 2030 and 111 in 2050, the main lever moving investment and dispatch away from fossil fuels. Target shares and subsidies: current or pledged policies enter as energy-share, capacity/generation and tax/subsidy constraints.
coreDrivers.emissionsTargets: No added constraint to 2030, then an end-of-century 2°C (67%) target with 80% of net-zero targets met, reached through a sharp post-2030 cut. MESSAGE applies net-zero GHG constraints by its 12 regions and approximates CO2-only targets with a 10-year-lagged GHG target.
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: MESSAGE minimises total system cost from investment, O&M and fuel costs. Exogenous declines (North America solar PV 853 to 374 US$2010/kW, 2020-2050) favour renewables, while cheap CCS keeps gas in the mix: wind and solar reach 73% of 2050 generation (Current Policies 31%). With carbon at 111 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050, the cost ranking tilts further to low-carbon options.
coreDrivers.investmentChange: Low-carbon power investment moves from 1.11% of GDP (MER) in 2020 to 0.70% in 2050, a decrease of 37%. MESSAGE's GDP grows faster than its power investment, so the share falls even where low-carbon investment rises in absolute terms.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: Shared SSP2 v3.0 population and GDP drive energy and material demand: 9.59 billion people in 2050 and GDP (MER) growing 3.85%/yr over 2020-2050. The assumptions are common to all NGFS scenarios; GDP differs from Current Policies only through transition costs (-0.51% in 2050).
coreDrivers.otherDrivers: Limited carbon dioxide removal: MESSAGE constrains BECCS availability by 2050, forcing deeper gross cuts and higher carbon prices (111 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050; total CCS 3747 Mt CO2/yr). It is a technology-availability limit, not a cost, policy or target, so no other driver fits. The 2030 switch is unanticipated, stranding capital built for a fossil recovery.

dependencies.dependency_description: Grid decarbonisation in Delayed Transition (MESSAGE) rests on the carbon price (2 US$2010/tCO2 in 2030, 111 in 2050). It lifts wind and solar from 9% of generation in 2020 to 73% in 2050 and cuts coal capacity to 72% of its 2020 level by 2040.

Power investment averages 1147 bn US$2010/yr over 2025-2050 (1.47x Current Policies), including 520 bn/yr for grids, and must be financed. A 2050 carbon price of 111 US$2010/tCO2 erodes unabated fossil plant profitability.

With wind and solar at 73% of 2050 generation, grids, storage and flexibility must absorb variable output. MESSAGE uses reliability coefficients and reaches 4874 GW of storage by 2050. Grid investment averages 520 bn US$2010/yr (2025-2050). No hourly dispatch is reported, so curtailment cannot be checked.

Power CCS captures 685 Mt CO2/yr in 2050 (0 Mt from bioenergy), so the pathway needs CCS at commercial scale; CCS cost differences between models drive large gaps in fossil generation. Storage of 4874 GW in 2050 relies on continued storage cost declines.

MESSAGE uses regional renewable potentials by quality and GLOBIOM biomass limited by food land. Power BECCS reaches 0 Mt CO2/yr and primary biomass 52 EJ in 2050, so land limits the negative-emission part of the power transition. Wind and solar at 73% of 204 EJ draw on the regional potentials.

Steel decarbonisation in Delayed Transition (MESSAGE) is steered only through economy-wide carbon pricing (111 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050) and emissions constraints; no steel-specific industrial policy is described. Steel emissions change by -23% over 2020-2050.

At 111 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050, fossil ironmaking costs more, favouring electricity (6.0 EJ) and hydrogen (0.0 EJ) in steel in 2050. No steel investment or unit-cost data are reported, so financing needs cannot be quantified.
MESSAGEix-Materials tracks recyclable steel scrap endogenously, so scrap availability limits secondary steelmaking in Delayed Transition (MESSAGE); scrap volumes are not reported.

byMetric.scopeLimitations: Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Derived Mt CO2 per EJ generated (1 EJ = 277.8 TWh). Scope 1 CO2 only; denominator is gross generation incl. CCS and bioenergy plants.
Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. CO2 only, Scope 1 (power-plant combustion, net of CCS); may include the electricity share of CHP.

Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Storage: one aggregate figure (Capacity|Electricity|Storage, GW) covering all storage; the source does not split it into battery, pumped hydro or hydrogen. Solar = PV + CSP; wind = onshore + offshore; CCS and non-CCS variants reported separately.

Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Gross secondary electricity (EJ/yr) by technology incl. CHP electricity; CCS and non-CCS variants reported. MESSAGE also reports transmission losses.
Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Derived generation shares; storage excluded (not a generating technology).
Overnight capital cost per kW by technology (geothermal, hydro, nuclear, solar PV, wind only; World aggregate 0, regional values only). No O&M, fuel or LCOE values.

granularity: By tech, part of value chain
byMetric.scopeLimitations: Annual investment, billion US$2010/yr. Post-processed variants may contain multi-model-average infill (NGFS Climate Scenarios Technical Documentation V5.0 (Nov 2024), p.82); native series used.
No lifetime values published; lifetimes fixed by technology, retirement endogenous. Inference relies on the coal capacity trajectory.
Derived t CO2(e) per t crude steel (sector emissions / Production|Steel, Mt/yr); primary and secondary routes combined; Scope 1 only.
Iron and steel modelled as one sector; ironmaking and steelmaking not separable. Energy-related CO2 only; Scope 1, excludes purchased electricity. Process-emission treatment not stated.
